summary: Timestamp-based session affinity reset during canary promote causes silent fallback to older variant
description:
Issue summary: During a planned canary promote (weight shift 20%->100%) for BrightLedger's dedicated deployment in eu-west, a subset (~1.4%) of in-flight sessions were observed to silently reroute to an older model variant. Impact: Affected requests returned lower-quality completions (reduced coherence) causing BrightLedger to report production regressions for end users. Environment: prod:eu-west, dedicated cluster rdw-ded-eu-07, canary promote initiated via Console rollout API.

Observed behavior: Around 2026-03-12T16:05:00Z — immediately after the final promote step — routing logs show a correlated spike in session-rebind events where session affinity tokens issued during the promote window were evaluated as expired by the edge-router. Those sessions were matched against fallback rules and sent to a compatible older variant (quantized v1) instead of the promoted primary. No 5xx errors were returned; traffic appeared healthy but outputs degraded for affected requests.

Why this ticket: Customer escalated at 16:45Z after customer QA detected regression in generated summaries. They requested incident triage, root cause, and mitigation/rollback if needed.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have a long-lived session pool with timestamp-based affinity tokens (TTL ~300s). 2) Start traffic against blue variant (open-7b-quantized-v1). 3) Initiate canary promote to green (open-7b-v1) using Console rollout API (weight 20->100 over 3 minutes). 4) Observe edge-router logs and session-rebind telemetry during final weight ramp. 5) Check per-session model routing decisions and compare affinity token timestamps vs server-side clock.

Notes: reproduce only reliably under steady-state traffic and when promote overlaps with token TTL expiry window.

2026-03-12T17:05Z | SRE - Marco Silva: Confirmed session_rebind spike coincident with promote completion. Initial hypothesis: timestamp-based affinity tokens expired during promote window, causing reconciler to treat sessions as unbound. Raising to eng-routing.

2026-03-12T18:01Z | Routing Eng - Evelyn Cho: Observed ~120ms clock skew between edge-proxy nodes and reconciler responsible for expiry checks. Skew combined with token TTL boundaries caused deterministic expiry on ~1% of tokens. Recommending mitigation: extend token grace window and force rebind back to promoted variant for affected sessions.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Session affinity tokens use token_issue_timestamp for TTL checks. During promote the reconciler evaluated token_age using its local clock which had small drift relative to edge-proxy. When token_age was near TTL boundary, drift pushed it over expiry leading to fallback routing. Evidence: session_rebind logs show token_age_seconds values clustered at ~TTL-7..+5 seconds at the time of promote. Clock skew measurement across nodes confirmed up to 220ms difference historically.

Additional observations: No errors in KV cache; routing decisions used fallback priority (compatible variant with same pipeline) instead of blocking. Console rollout does not currently coordinate token refresh for active sessions when promote occurs.

Correlated linked issues: SUP-42156 (canary affinity loss during hotfix cutover) shows similar symptoms but with different root cause (cache drain timing).
workaround:
Immediate: 1) For customers who cannot tolerate any regressions, instruct Console to pause promote and perform explicit rolling restart of edge-proxies to refresh affinity tokens prior to promote. 2) Support can trigger targeted rebind job to refresh tokens for affected session IDs (temporary) via admin route.

Planned: hotfix to add clock-skew grace in TTL eval (deployed as control-plane change) and add a promote coordination step that issues new affinity tokens for active sessions when finalizing a promote.
resolution_notes: Mitigation in prod: control-plane hotfix to include 500ms grace window applied 2026-03-14 08:30Z to eu-west cluster. Short-term reduction in misroutes from ~1.4% to ~0.02%. Follow-ups: (1) implement promote-time token refresh in route-manager (PR opened), (2) cross-node clock-sync alert to detect RTT/clock drift >200ms. Will keep ticket open until promote-token-refresh and additional e2e tests land.
next_steps: 1) Eng: merge promote-token-refresh PR and add e2e that simulates TTL boundary promotes. 2) SRE: create automated monitor for session_rebind rate per-promote and alert at >0.1%. 3) Support: notify BrightLedger of mitigation and schedule postmortem review with customer next week.
